title: Landmaschinen: Claas investiert 6,5 Mio. Euro, nicht in Harsewinkel
content: # Landmaschinen: Claas investiert 6,5 Mio. Euro, nicht in Harsewinkel. **Claas geht von einem steigenden Absatz für diese Landmaschine aus und vergrößert ein wichtiges Produktionswerk in Frankreich.**. Der Landtechnikhersteller Claas ist vor allem für seine Mähdrescher und Feldhäcksler, aber auch für Grünlandtechnik und Traktoren bekannt. 2023 modernisierte das Unternehmen für 44 Mio. Euro die Mähdrescherproduktion in Harsewinkel. Jetzt steht ein Investitionsvolumen von 6,5 Mio. Euro an. ## Traktoren von Claas: Vor über 20 Jahren begann der Einstieg. Aus den Traktoren Renault Celtis, Ares und Atles wurde über die Jahre Claas Arion und Axion. ## Le Mans ist die Heimat von den Traktoren Claas Arion und Axion. In Le Mans produziert Claas alle Standard-Traktoren (kein Xerion) ab 75 PS und investierte seit der Übernahme rund 80 Millionen Euro, beispielsweise in eine neue Kabinen-Vormontage, eine Montagelinie, eine neue Lackieranlage sowie in ein Besucher- und Schulungszentrum. 2025 konnten von den großen Konzernen neben AGCO nur noch Claas Marktanteile in Deutschland bei Traktoren ausbauen.

title: The KLAAS Agricultural Machinery Manufacturer in Harsewinkel
content: We had some rain on and off all day. Next we drove to a town about 30 min away called Harsewinkel where there is a HUGE factory that makes farm equipment and columbines. The tour of the facility was long and detailed. Sadly, this is a vacation period for all of the 12,000 workers, so all of the assembly lines were empty of employees at work. This little knotting device was the beginning of all of this:. Founded in 1913 by August Claas, CLAAS is a family business and one of the market and technology leaders in harvesting technology. The beginnings of the company go back to 1887, when Franz Claas founded a company in Clarholz for the production of milk centrifuges. The official foundation of the company took place in 1913, when the son of Franz Claas, August Claas, informed the responsible office in Herzebrock that he was manufacturing straw binders with two locksmiths and one unskilled worker.

title: A Visit to Claas HQ in Harsewinkel
content: # A Visit to Claas HQ in Harsewinkel. ## In November a trip to Harsewinkel, Germany shows the place where Claas was founded and maintains at its worldwide headquarters today. Harsewinkel, Germany is the worldwide hub for the international farm machinery company Claas. Started by August Claas, today the company makes self-propelled combines for corn, soybeans, rice and small grains; self-propelled forage harvesters; haying equipment; and tractors. Claas has invested in new facilities in Omaha, Neb., Russia, and India with the purpose to producing machines where they will be used. The manufacturing facilities there produce self-propelled forage harvesters, Xerion machines, and combines for western Europe as well as threshing modules for other markets. It takes one day’s time to assembly a combine, and the factory produces 18 to 19 combines a day. There is a one assembly line dedicated to Jaguar forage harvesters, and there are 16 machines on the assembly at a time.

title: Harsewinkel | CLAAS
content: We manufacture and assemble at over ten production plants worldwide. Our main factory in Harsewinkel works closely with our international sites—on equal footing—to ensure the highest quality standards at all times. Minus 4 degrees Fahrenheit and sleet: when Lisane Volkeri arrived at the CLAAS factory in Omaha, Nebraska, in January 2018, it was so cold that the entrance door had frozen shut. They had to prepare the Omaha factory for the full-scale production of a new series of the LEXION large combine harvester—model numbers 8900–5300—just a few months after the prototype had been assembled for the first time in Harsewinkel. The goal was to produce the machines in the American factory to exactly the same standards as the main production plant within two years—even though Omaha is nearly 4,400 miles away from Harsewinkel as the crow flies. Bernd Schapmann, manager of the main combine harvester assembly line in Harsewinkel, is responsible for ensuring that CLAAS quality standards are the same worldwide.
